Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:10:1.english: And furthermore, what is [the meaning of] “this one chooses” - For it implies that this is the law.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:12:1.hebrew: יצא דין אמת לאמיתו - דצייתי בעלי דינין, דסבר החייב: הרי אני בעצמי ביררתי האחד, ואם היה יכול להפך בזכותי היה מהפך. והדיינין בעצמן נוחה דעתן להפך בזכות שניהן, מפני ששניהם ביררום:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:12:1.english: A true judgment will emerge in its truth - For the litigants will accept [the verdict], as the liable party reasons: Behold, I myself selected the one [judge], and if he were able to argue in my favor, he would have argued [in my favor]. And the judges themselves are favorably disposed to argue in favor of both of them, because both of them selected them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:14:1.hebrew: אא"כ יודעין מי חותם עמהן - שמא יחתמו עמהם עד אחד פסול, ומבטל עדות כולם, ונמצאו אלו בושים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:14:1.english: Unless they know who is signing with them - Lest an unfit witness sign with them and invalidate the testimony of all of them, and these [witnesses] will be disgraced.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:14:2.hebrew: ורבנן אית להו דרב יהודה - הלכך, דעת הדיינין בעינן, שיבררו מי ישב עמהם — אדם הגון:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:14:2.english: And the Rabbis accept [the ruling] of Rav Yehuda - Therefore, we require the consent of the judges, that they select who will sit with them — [to ensure he is] a worthy person.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:16:1.english: And they would not join a meal, etc. - For it is disgraceful for Torah scholars to sit next to an ignoramus at a meal.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:17:1.hebrew: זה פוסל דיינו של זה וזה פוסל דיינו של זה - יכול לומר לו: "לא אדון לפניו". (ע"כ):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:17:1.english: This [litigant] can disqualify the judge of that [litigant], and that [litigant] can disqualify the judge of this [litigant] - He can say to him: "I will not be judged before him." (Thus far.)

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:1:1.hebrew: מתני'. זה בורר לו אחד - משמע: זה בורר לו ב"ד אחד, שהן ג', וזה אחד — הרי ששה, ושניהם בוררין להם עוד אחד — הרי ט'. והיינו דקא מתמה: מאי זה בורר כו' — הא בתלתא סגי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:1:1.english: The Mishnah: This [litigant] chooses one for himself - [This] implies: This [litigant] chooses one court for himself, which is three [judges], and that [litigant chooses] one [court] — behold, [there are] six; and both of them choose one more [court] for themselves — behold, [there are] nine. And that is why [the Gemara] wonders: What is [the meaning of] “This [litigant] chooses, etc.” — behold, three [judges] are sufficient!

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:20:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר אבל אם היו כשרין - שאינם קרובין ולא פסולין, אף ע"פ שהן יושבי קרנות — נעשו כמומחין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:20:1.english: This is what [the Mishnah] is saying: But if they were fit - That they are neither relatives nor disqualified; even though they are people who sit at street corners, they are treated like experts.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:23:1.hebrew: עד שיקבל עליו בפני ב"ד מומחה - אלמא, במומחין מודה ר"מ:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:23:1.english: Until he accepts upon himself before an expert court - Evidently, Rabbi Meir concedes regarding expert [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:24:1.english: But aren’t witnesses like experts - If they are not relatives or [otherwise] disqualified.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:27:1.english: That they accepted him upon themselves as two - At the beginning of their claims, they accepted him upon themselves as two [witnesses].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:28:1.hebrew: נאמן עלי וכו' - בדיינין קמיירי, מדקתני ג' רועי בקר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:28:1.english: “[He is] trusted to me,” etc. - [The Mishnah] is dealing with judges, since it teaches: “Three cattle herders.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:5:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר כשזה בורר לו ב"ד אחד וזה בורר לו ב"ד אחד - וכל אחד פוסל אותו ב"ד שבירר חבירו, ואינו רוצה לדון לפניו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:5:1.english: This is what [the Mishnah] is saying: When this [litigant] chooses one court for himself, and that [litigant] chooses one court for himself - And each one disqualifies the court that his fellow chose, and does not wish to be judged before it.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:5:2.hebrew: שניהן בוררין להם אחד - כלומר, אין יכולין לכוף זה את זה, אלא בוררין ב"ד שיתרצו בו שניהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:5:2.english: Both of them choose one for themselves - That is to say, they cannot compel one another; rather, they choose a court that both of them agree to.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:1.hebrew: ואפי' לוה מצי מעכב - בתמיה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:1.english: And can even a debtor restrict - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:2.hebrew: והאמר ר"א - לקמן בסוף פירקין (סנהדרין דף לא:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:2.english: But doesn’t Rabbi Elazar say - [This is stated] later, at the end of our chapter (Sanhedrin 31b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:3.hebrew: לא שנו - אחד אמר נידון כאן, ואחד אמר נלך לבית הוועד — כופין אותו והולך לבית הוועד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:3.english: They only taught - [That which was stated: If] one said, "Let us be judged here," and one said, "Let us go to the house of assembly," they compel him and he goes to the house of assembly.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:6:4.english: [Only when the creditor says: "Let us go to the place of assembly"] - For "the borrower is a slave to the lender."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:7:1.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan says - Later in our discussion.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:7:2.hebrew: בערכאות שבסוריא - שלא היו בקיאין בדין תורה, הלכך אפי' לוה מצי מעכב:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:7:2.english: In the courts in Syria - For they were not knowledgeable in Torah law; therefore, even the debtor can object.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23a:8:1.english: The court of Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda - For both of them [were] in the same place.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23a:12:1.hebrew: כדי שיצא הדין לאמיתו - פירש הריב"ן, שאפילו החייב יפרע ברצון ויאמר: "קושטא דייני, שאני בעצמי ביררתי האחד, ואם היה יכול להפך בזכותי — היה מהפך". לפום ריהטא משמע כך הפירוש: שמתוך שבירר זה שלו, וזה שלו, השלישי — יצא הדין לאמיתו בלא עוות, שיהא הענין שקול, ולא ירבו מהפכין לחובה על מהפכין לזכות, ולא להפך:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23a:12:1.english: "So that the true judgment will emerge" - The Rivan explained that even the liable party will pay willingly and say: "They have judged truthfully, for I myself chose the one [judge], and had he been able to argue in my favor, he would have argued." At first glance, the explanation seems to be this: that since this [litigant] chose his [judge] and that [litigant] chose his [judge], [and both chose] the third, the judgment will emerge in its truth without distortion, so that the matter will be balanced, and those arguing for liability will not outnumber those arguing for exoneration, nor the reverse.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23a:4:1.hebrew: מאי זה בורר לו אחד וזה בורר לו אחד - פ"ה דמשמע דלהוו ט'. כיצד? זה בורר לו ב"ד אחד, הרי ג'; וזה בורר לו ב"ד אחד, הרי ששה; ושניהם בוררים להם ב"ד אחר, הרי ט'. ולהכי מתמה: "בתלתא סגי". ולא נהירא, שהרי משמעות הלשון אינו כן; דא"כ, ה"ל להקשות בהדיא: "הא גופא קשיא, רישא אסיפא — אמרת: דיני ממונות בשלשה, אלמא בג' סגי, והדר קאמר דצריך ט'!?" ונ"ל דאף בתחילה היה יודע, כמו שמפרש אח"כ, שזה פוסל ב"ד של חבירו וזה פוסל ב"ד של חבירו, ולא ישבו כ"א ג' אחרונים, כדקאמר המתרץ. ולא פריך אלא מלישנא דמתני', דקתני: "זה בורר ב"ד וחבירו כן"; ולהכי פריך: "מאי זה בורר לו אחד?", כלומר: לא סגי בלאו הכי? ומשני: "כשזה בורר", כלומר: אין חובה ודאי לעשות כן, אלא מתני' מיירי אם אירע כך:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23a:4:1.english: What [is the meaning of] "this [litigant] chooses one and that [litigant] chooses one": - Rashi explained that [this] implies that there should be nine [judges]. How so? This [litigant] chooses one court for himself — behold, three; and that [litigant] chooses one court for himself — behold, six; and both of them choose another court for themselves — behold, nine. And for this reason [the Gemara] wonders: Isn't it sufficient with three? But [this] does not appear [correct], for the phrasing does not imply this; for if so, [the Gemara] should have explicitly challenged: This itself is difficult, [from] the beginning [of the tractate] to the end [here] — you said [that] monetary laws [are judged] by three, which shows that three are sufficient, and then it says that nine are required!? Rather, it seems to me that even initially [the questioner] knew, as [the Gemara] explains afterwards, that this [litigant] disqualifies the court of the other and that [litigant] disqualifies the court of the other, and none sat except the final three [judges], as the answerer states. And [the Gemara] only objected from the language of the Mishnah, which teaches: This [litigant] chooses a court and his fellow [litigant does] likewise; and for this reason it asks: "What [is the meaning of] 'this [litigant] chooses one for himself'?", that is to say: Is it not sufficient without this? And it answers: "When this [litigant] chooses...", that is to say: There is certainly no obligation to do so, but rather the Mishnah is dealing [with a case where] it happened like this.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23a:8:1.hebrew: כגון בי דינא דרב הונא ורב חסדא דאמר ליה מאי קמטרחנא לך וכו' - פירש הקונטרס שהיו במקום אחד. ולא נהירא; דהא אמרי' (עירובין סב:) דרב חסדא לא היה מורה לפני רב הונא אפי' ביעתא בכותחא, וכ"ש דדין לא היה עושה בפניו. ונ"ל שהיו סמוכים זה לזה, חוץ לג' פרסאות:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23a:8:1.english: "Such as the court of Rav Huna and Rav Chisda, where he says to him: 'How am I burdening you?' etc." - Rashi explained that they were in one place. But this does not appear correct, for we say (Eruvin 62b) that Rav Chisda would not issue a halakhic ruling in the presence of Rav Huna, even [regarding] an egg in kutach, and all the more so he would not judge a case in his presence! And it appears to me that they were close to each other, [yet] outside three parasangs [of each other].
